gaps: Aesthetic/lifestyle-vibe fit (adjacency to video games/AI/cyberware/anime, everyday routine utility) is a qualitative judgment the brief/critique stages should make from the gathered project characteristics — it is not the kind of claim that benefits from further source corroboration, and only generic/weak search results (TikTok, tutorial roundups) exist for 'cyberpunk desk companion' as a category; this should be treated as a design/rationale judgment call downstream, not an unresolved factual gap.

Detailed per-chapter build-phase mapping (which project phase maps to which specific confirmed chapter, in what order) was intentionally left to the research-brief stage per the plan's division of labor — source gathering confirmed the chapter structure and the projects' real technical characteristics (DOF, kinematics type, control stack, dynamics/gearing relevance) needed to support that mapping, but did not itself produce the final mapping table.
summary: PDF text/TOC extraction tools were unavailable at the start of this round (no pdftotext/pdftoppm), so poppler was installed via Homebrew during this round, after which pdftotext read the actual PDF's front matter directly (pages 1-9 contents, 14-18 preface) — no fallback to the public syllabus was needed. Confirmed ground truth: 644-page 'updated first edition' preprint (Dec 2019, Cambridge University Press 2017 original) with 13 numbered chapters (Preview; Configuration Space; Rigid-Body Motions; Forward Kinematics; Velocity Kinematics and Statics; Inverse Kinematics; Kinematics of Closed Chains; Dynamics of Open Chains; Trajectory Generation; Motion Planning; Robot Control; Grasping and Manipulation; Wheeled Mobile Robots), 4 appendices (Useful Formulas; Other Rotation Representations; Denavit-Hartenberg Parameters; Optimization and Lagrange Multipliers), bibliography, and index, plus the authors' own stated prerequisite guidance (Ch.2-6 as sequential 'minimum essentials', named example course paths through the remaining chapters). Also gathered 4 candidate hobbyist projects, each with 3-4 independent corroborating sources covering real-world buildability, cost, and community activity: (1) SO-ARM100/101 desktop robot arm (Hugging Face LeRobot ecosystem, ~$115-230, thousands of builders); (2) LeKiwi mobile manipulator (SO-ARM101 arm + holonomic Kiwi-drive wheeled base, ~$660, combines arm and wheeled-robot chapters including mobile manipulation); (3) Sawppy rover (rocker-bogie wheeled Mars-rover replica derived from NASA JPL's open-source rover, <$500, active Hackaday build-log community); (4) Petoi Bittle (9-DOF open-source OpenCat quadruped robot pet/companion, ~$200-225, 2,052-backer Kickstarter plus ongoing active product line).
